# Powers and roots

Raising to a power, square and cube roots, and the hypotenuse.

<h2 id="cbrt"><code>Cbrt</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Cbrt(x: float64) -> float64
pub func Cbrt(x: float32) -> float32
```

Computes the real cube root of `x`.
The error is at most one ulp. Negative inputs produce negative roots, a signed zero or infinity returns itself, and
a NaN remains a NaN.

| Overload                               | Summary                                                    |
| -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `pub func Cbrt(x: float64) -> float64` | Computes the real cube root of `x`.                        |
| `pub func Cbrt(x: float32) -> float32` | Computes the real cube root of `x` at `float32` precision. |

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Math/Src/Cbrt.rux#L12)

**Parameters**

| Name | Type                  | Description                       |
| ---- | --------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| `x`  | `float64` / `float32` | value whose cube root is computed |

**Returns**: the real cube root of `x`

<h2 id="hypot"><code>Hypot</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Hypot(x: float64, y: float64) -> float64
pub func Hypot(x: float32, y: float32) -> float32
```

Computes the Euclidean length `Sqrt(x * x + y * y)` without intermediate overflow or underflow.
The error is at most one ulp. An infinity in either argument returns positive infinity even when the other is a NaN;
otherwise a NaN remains a NaN.

| Overload                                            | Summary                                                                                         |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `pub func Hypot(x: float64, y: float64) -> float64` | Computes the Euclidean length `Sqrt(x * x + y * y)` without intermediate overflow or underflow. |
| `pub func Hypot(x: float32, y: float32) -> float32` | Computes the Euclidean length of `(x, y)` at `float32` precision.                               |

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Math/Src/Hypot.rux#L13)

**Parameters**

| Name | Type                  | Description                |
| ---- | --------------------- | -------------------------- |
| `x`  | `float64` / `float32` | first Cartesian component  |
| `y`  | `float64` / `float32` | second Cartesian component |

**Returns**: the non-negative length of `(x, y)`

<h2 id="pow"><code>Pow</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Pow(x: float64, y: float64) -> float64
pub func Pow(x: float32, y: float32) -> float32
```

Raises `x` to the power `y`.
The error is at most one ulp. A negative base requires an integer exponent; otherwise the result is a NaN.
[`PowInteger`](/docs/api/math/powers#pow-integer) is both faster and able to preserve exact results when the exponent is an integer.

| Overload                                          | Summary                                             |
| ------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `pub func Pow(x: float64, y: float64) -> float64` | Raises `x` to the power `y`.                        |
| `pub func Pow(x: float32, y: float32) -> float32` | Raises `x` to the power `y` at `float32` precision. |

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Math/Src/Pow.rux#L164)

**Parameters**

| Name | Type                  | Description |
| ---- | --------------------- | ----------- |
| `x`  | `float64` / `float32` | base        |
| `y`  | `float64` / `float32` | exponent    |

**Returns**: `x` raised to `y`

<h2 id="pow-integer"><code>PowInteger</code></h2>

```rux
pub func PowInteger(base: float64, exponent: int64) -> float64
pub func PowInteger(base: float32, exponent: int64) -> float32
```

`base` raised to the integer power `exponent`.
A zero exponent gives one for every base, including zero and a NaN, which is the same rule [`Pow`](/docs/api/math/powers#pow) follows: the empty
product is one. A negative exponent takes the reciprocal at the end rather than dividing as it goes, which keeps the
intermediates as large as possible and loses the least.

| Overload                                                         | Summary                                                               |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `pub func PowInteger(base: float64, exponent: int64) -> float64` | `base` raised to the integer power `exponent`.                        |
| `pub func PowInteger(base: float32, exponent: int64) -> float32` | Raises `base` to the integer power `exponent` at `float32` precision. |

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Math/Src/PowInteger.rux#L17)

**Parameters**

| Name       | Type                  | Description    |
| ---------- | --------------------- | -------------- |
| `base`     | `float64` / `float32` | value to raise |
| `exponent` | `int64`               | integer power  |

**Returns**: `base` raised to `exponent`

<h2 id="sqrt"><code>Sqrt</code></h2>

```rux
pub func Sqrt(x: float32) -> float32
pub func Sqrt(x: float64) -> float64
```

Computes the correctly rounded square root of `x` at `float32` precision.
A signed zero, positive infinity, or NaN passes through; a negative finite value returns a NaN.

| Overload                               | Summary                                                                   |
| -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `pub func Sqrt(x: float32) -> float32` | Computes the correctly rounded square root of `x` at `float32` precision. |
| `pub func Sqrt(x: float64) -> float64` | Computes the correctly rounded square root of `x`.                        |

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Math/Src/Sqrt.rux#L18)

**Parameters**

| Name | Type                  | Description                         |
| ---- | --------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| `x`  | `float32` / `float64` | value whose square root is computed |

**Returns**: the non-negative square root of `x`, or a NaN when `x` is negative
